text:
tyler (Support): FYI we've got an escalated ticket from Acme: reported tail latency spike after last night's deploy. They see p99 jump ~5x for text-generation API. Rolling to you @eng-oncall.
jen (SRE): thanks. do we have a sample request id or time window? any auth/billing errors too?
tyler (Support): customer provided a trace: request_id=rc-9b3f, window 2023-11-20T02:14Z-02:26Z. No billing errors in the logs they shared. Attachments show retries and a few 502s.

matt (Runtime): I pulled our request logs for that range:
```
metric: redwood.api.request.latency_ms
filter: model:open-llama-13b, route:/v1/generate
agg: p50/p95/p99 by minute
```
we see a p99 spike starting ~02:15Z that lines up with deploy-bot action: deploy-bot: "canary promote v2.3.7 -> all" at 02:12Z :deploy:
deploy-bot: promoted canary v2.3.7 to cluster=us-west-2, pool=hosted-gen

alvin (Observability): dashboard timeseries (panel id 112) shows p99 spike, but raw histogram for the same window doesn't show the same shape. I suspect rollup vs histogram bucketization mismatch. The rollup query computes quantiles from rollup summaries, not raw events.

nora (Support): customer insists they saw many 5-10s responses; their screenshot shows >20s in some logs.

jen (SRE): can we repro high latency in the infra? checking pod restarts and GPU metrics. matt, did runtime change kernel selection logic in v2.3.7?\

matt (Runtime): v2.3.7 included a change: prefer int8 quantized kernels for seq_len > 1024 if memory pressure low. Also changed request routing to favor packed batching. Could increase head-of-line wait if batching thresholds changed. I'll revert the routing change on a canary instance.

alvin (Observability): to be precise on the metric mismatch: our p99 panel uses a rollup dataset (1m rollups) that stores quantile estimates per minute. The histogram panel uses raw-event bucketing with boundaries: [0,10,50,100,250,500,1000,2000,..] ms. If many outliers exceed the largest bucket they get clipped or show as overflow, and quantile estimation from rollups can amplify short spikes.

tyler (Support): customer logs include this snippet:
```
[2023-11-20T02:16:12Z] rc-9b3f: latency=8.2s status=200
[2023-11-20T02:16:13Z] rc-9b3f: latency=9.9s status=200
[2023-11-20T02:16:17Z] rc-9b3f: latency=24.5s status=200
```

jen (SRE): those look real. the big question: are these client-side retries piling up or server-side inference stalls? Look at backend queues (redis/batch queue depth) and GPU utilization.

matt (Runtime): initial check: GPU utilization was normal, but batch queue depth spiked from <10 to ~220 for ~6 minutes starting 02:15Z. Batches were waiting longer due to the new packing logic—we hit a pathological request pattern (many small synchronous requests from a single customer), so the packer waited to fill batches.

jen (SRE): that explains 8-24s tails. mitigation options:
- roll back packing change on hosted pool (hotfix)
- lower packer max wait threshold for canary
- enable per-customer bypass for small synchronous requests

alvin (Observability): also let's reconcile dashboards accurately so support/customer can see consistent numbers. Proposed short-term: add a raw-events p99 panel (no rollup) for that route and link it in the incident report. Long-term: normalize quantile derivation between rollup and histogram. I'll open a ticket: OBS-314.

nora (Support): I'll send Acme an interim reply: saying we identified a canary packing change that induced queueing and we're rolling a mitigation. ask them for any additional request_ids.

matt (Runtime): deploying hotfix: reduced packer wait from 50ms -> 10ms on hosted-gen pool. rolling now (will post when done). :worker:

deploy-bot: hotfix rollout started: hotfix/pack-wait-10ms -> hosted-gen (canary 3 -> 10) at 02:34Z

matt (Runtime): hotfix applied to all hosts in hosted-gen by 02:43Z. monitoring shows batch queue depth back to normal and p99 trending down.

alvin (Observability): updated dashboard panel 112 to include raw p99 and annotated the 02:12Z deploy. saved a permalink and attached to the support ticket.

jen (SRE): closing loop: root cause = packing change + unlucky request distribution from Acme causing long queuing. mitigation = hotfix + add guard for small synchronous clients. follow-ups: runtime to submit PR with a packing adaptive threshold, obs to standardize quantile sources, support to confirm with customer.

tyler (Support): Acme replied: thanks, p99 back to normal in our monitors. they asked whether anything changed to request timeout behavior — I told them no change to timeouts, just reduced server-side batching wait. :thumbsup:

nora (Support): marking the ticket resolved after customer confirms. adding notes and linking OBS-314 and RUNTIME-449 in the ticket.

jen (SRE): good job everyone. postmortem optional but recommended if we see recurrence. :eyes:
